summary: Eleven days after Barbara wrote 'i really want to continue working together, i just need to see some changes because where the numbers are right now isn’t sustainable for me', not one person at ALTR has replied to that sentence. No call was written up, no plan was posted, no number was ever shown to her. That is the headline of this window and it has not moved. What did happen: Meta support finally woke up. Vivek sent nine messages — more than his previous eight weeks combined — and for the first time gave her real direction ('Ma’am don’t appeal', 'Will unban these accounts one by one'). Derrek stayed in the chat instead of vanishing again and on Sep 19 claimed a result: 'Yes we got both of your backup accounts back'. She answered 'AMAZING THANK YOU!'. Within eighteen hours that claim fell apart in public — a recovered account was down again ('already 🥺😭', Sep 20), she asked 'did anyone even log into that one or what happened', and then said plainly 'i never got a “you’re back on instagram” email for my @barbarasilvanew account either so i’m not sure what the other backup that was recovered was but i don’t think it was mine'. Nobody has answered any of those three messages, five days later. Her main account @thebrazilianfitbarbie is still gone — eight days now, against Derrek's 'It might be a few days' on Sep 17. On Sep 20 she asked directly whether the rumoured Tuesday unban covered her, 'we are good for my main right?... i just wanna make sure im good and don’t need to figure out a back up plan'. Tuesday came and went in silence. Mayson asked Vivek 'How long do you it will take?' on Sep 21 and got no answer at all. Barbara then did ALTR's diagnostic work for the second time in a month, producing her own root-cause theory — 'can you work on threads first ? i have a feeling this is the could be the root cause for all the other problems' — and Derrek said 'We will check'. Nothing since. The window ends badly. Vivek asked her to log into the suspended account and screenshot it; she raised a safety objection three times — 'i’m sorta nervous to log in on this phone', '@ofwizz what should i do should i use this phone to log in', 'I only own three phones, so I’m just scared to login because each phone is already attached to an account' — and nobody replied. That was 07:29 on Sep 22. She has not said a word since: roughly three days of client silence, an entirely dead Sep 23, and a Sep 24 that contained only Mayson chasing Vivek internally. Billing did settle: Stephski chased the $1,683.12 on day six with the pause-of-work deadline attached — which last week's report explicitly said not to do while her account was down — and Barbara apologised ('Oh hey sorry yes it slipped my mind my bad!') and paid it inside two hours. Invoice #4 is now fully paid. Four invoices, four paid in full, zero disputes. And two services went dark: Michelle sent zero messages for the second consecutive week, so the leak-removal report is now seventeen days missing, and Mica Vecco — last week's best performer, whose inspo cadence this report certified as fixed — sent nothing at all, breaking it at the first test.

health.rationale: Down 4 from 42 (2026-09-18), the lowest score recorded on this account, and down 34 from the 72 at first measurement nine weeks ago. There is genuine operational improvement in here and it is worth being precise about it: Vivek finally engaged (nine messages after weeks of near-silence, and actual instruction rather than 'Will do it today'), Derrek stayed present across Sep 19, 20 and 22 rather than disappearing as he did for 36 days in August, Olivia executed her Sep 17 free-page commitment inside four days, and Barbara settled the $1,683.12 balance in full with no dispute. On responsiveness and effort this is not a bad week. The score still falls, for five reasons. (1) THE CENTRAL QUESTION IS ELEVEN DAYS OLD AND STILL UNANSWERED. Her Sep 14 retention message asked for numbers and a clear plan. Neither exists. Mayson's offered Sep 15 call has still never been referenced again by anyone. In 67 days she has never been shown a single metric. (2) THE MAIN ACCOUNT IS STILL DEAD at 8 days against 'a few days', and her direct Sep 20 question about the Tuesday unban was never answered — Mayson's own 'How long do you it will take?' was also ignored by Vivek. (3) THE ONE DELIVERY CLAIM COLLAPSED IN PUBLIC. Derrek said both backups were recovered on Sep 19; by Sep 20 one was down again and she stated she does not believe the other was ever hers. Three messages disputing the claim have gone unanswered for five days. A recovery the client does not believe happened is worse than no recovery. (4) THE CLIENT HAS GONE QUIET. Her last message was a frightened, three-times-repeated question about whether it was safe to log in on her own phone — unanswered. She has said nothing for roughly three days; Sep 23 was completely dead and Sep 24 contained only internal chatter. On an account that spent August and September escalating loudly, silence is not calm. (5) BOTH SURVIVING SERVICES STOPPED. Michelle: second straight zero-message week, leak report 17 days missing, and Barbara — who thanked her for it six weeks running — has stopped asking for it. Mica Vecco: zero messages, inspo cadence broken 10 days after this report certified it as fixed. Held above the mid-30s only by Vivek's re-engagement, Derrek's continued presence, Olivia's follow-through and a clean payment record.
